title: client-surge-bridge-notes-ashwin
content:
Context:
- Quick scratchpad for the client-initiated bridge (Acct: NovaPay) — intermittent 5xxs and long tail latency on hosted API since 2026-03-07 21:10 PDT. Customer reports page loads slow and some front-end timeouts. They see errors only on model 'redwood-13b-v2-q4' routes.
- Primary ask from customer: immediate mitigation + clear timeline for full resolution. They have legal/compliance review kicking off; high visibility.
- Current bridge owner: Ashwin (me). Secondary: Maya (SRE). SE: Diego. AE: Priya.

Immediate goals for bridge (prep checklist):
- Protect customer traffic and limit impact: routing fallback plan, temporary rate limits, and aborts for long-running requests.
- Gather forensics: logs (proxy + runtime), tail of model server logs, recent rollout history, bucketed latency percentiles by route and sequence-length.
- Stakeholder comms: Acknowledge, ETA for first update 30m, hourly updates thereafter until stable.
- Prepare readout for PM/CS leadership at 14:30 PT tomorrow (include timeline, impact, root cause hypothesis, mitigation plan).

Agenda for first 15-minute sync (standup-style):
1) Quick tl;dr of customer impact (me) — who sees errors, frequency, sample trace.
2) Live data (Maya) — p50/p95/p99 pre/post 21:10, error rate spike, any correlated infra events.
3) Model/runtime status (Diego) — current processes, recent rollouts, config drift, quantization flags.
4) Mitigation options (all) — immediate and medium term.
5) Owner assignments & comm cadence (me).

Data to pull before joining (priority order):
- Request traces for failing requests (trace ids sample set) — from observability/trace UI.
- Token-level breakdown: where time is being spent (kernel? KV cache?).
- Model container restarts OOM? GPU memory spike graphs (NVIDIA/DCGM). Check last 48h.
- Recent deploys: who merged to serving-runtime or model catalog in last 72h (check PRs & release tags).
- Any config changes to batching or prefix caching policy for this tenant.

Hypotheses (initial, quick):
- Hypothesis A: rolling model variant rollout with new kernel selection introduced perf regression for long sequences. Evidence to look for: partial rollout in feature flags, PRs mentioning kernel selection.
- Hypothesis B: caching bug — KV cache invalidation leading to repeated full-attention passes. Evidence: increasing tokens/time per request as conversation progresses.
- Hypothesis C: upstream infra (network/storage) flakiness causing retries that amplify tail latency.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
- 0 (fastest): Route customer traffic to a stable model variant (redwood-13b-v2-legacy) and pin until root cause confirmed. Pros: fastest, minimal infra changes. Cons: small perf/cost delta.
- 1: Enable aggressive per-request short-circuit (cut generation at 256 tokens) for this account. Slightly user-visible.
- 2: Toggle off the recent kernel optimization flag (if feature-flagged) for affected hosts.
- 3: Scale up dedicated pool for this customer (if on dedicated) — time to spin up matters.

Communications templates (first message to customer - 30m):
- Acknowledge receipt, confirm we’re on a bridge, list initial mitigations we will attempt (routing + logs), set next update in 30m. Keep language calm, non-technical summary + technical note for their SRE.

Immediate action items (owner / due):
- Ashwin: open formal incident ticket (JIRA-14192) + post initial customer message (due: +10m). DONE.
- Maya: collect p95/p99 latency graphs + attach traces (due: +20m). IN PROGRESS.
- Diego: check recent model-serving PRs/rollouts, validate container restarts/oom (due: +20m). IN PROGRESS.
- Priya: alert AE/Customer success leadership, prep backup comms (legal might ask) (due: +30m). IN PROGRESS.
- Ops: create a pinned fallback route in router config to legacy variant (owner: ops-team) (due: +40m).

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Keep updates very short: what changed, who owns next, ETA. No long retros in bridge updates.
- If routing fallback chosen, validate: 1) canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metrics check at each step, 2) confirm logs show requests hitting intended model.
- Watch out for correlated sign: COST spike on token billing indicates unexpectedly higher token usage (could be infinite loop in prompt building).

Follow-up / actions after stable (post-mortem skeleton):
- Timeline: what happened, when, who changed what.
- Root cause analysis: reproduce dev-only minimal test case that triggers regression.
- Remediation: fix kernel selection / cache bug + unit/integration test to prevent regressions.
- Rollout policy change: require perf smoke tests on model variants before canary rollout (add to release checklist).
- Customer remediation: SLA credit discussion + incident summary.

Open questions to resolve in next 2 hours:
- Is model variant rollout automated via CI or gated? (Diego)
- Any infra maintenance that overlapped? (Maya)
- Does customer use custom prompt engineering or unusually long sequences? (AE)

Prep for readout (deliverables):
- One-page timeline for execs (impact numbers, mitigation chosen, ETA for full fix).
- Short technical appendix: sample traces (anonymized), kernel flags, mem/GPU graphs.
- Proposed customer-facing postmortem (drafted by me + Priya).

Scratch thoughts (do not share verbatim):
- If this is a kernel perf regression, we should consider temporary auto-fallback for all customers to legacy kernel when p99 latency > X ms for 10m window.
- Keep legal looped only if asked; AE to own contractual language.

Next sync cadence: 20 minutes from now, then hourly until stable.

-- ashwin
